standard_prerequisites.name: Ordinals as the set of smaller ordinals
standard_prerequisites.use: Cited at line 1085 to read alpha in beta as beta's initial segment at alpha.

core_obligations: Setup (proof lines 1074-1078): write ordtype(A,<) = alpha, ordtype(B,lessdot) = beta, and fix an isomorphism f : beta -> B.

Chain of equivalences (lines 1079-1084): alpha in beta iff the restriction f|alpha maps alpha isomorphically onto B_{f(alpha)}; iff A is isomorphic to that segment; iff A is isomorphic to B_b for some b in B.
Endorsement of the chain (line 1085): each equivalence rests on the four named lemmas of the unit, listed by the author at the end of the display.
proof_roadmap: Fix the ordinal names alpha, beta and a representing isomorphism f.
Rewrite ordinal membership as an isomorphism statement about restrictions of f.
Translate the target segment via surjectivity of f into some B_b.
Note the converse direction is the same chain read backwards.
difficulty_reason: A corollary packaging the segment machinery of the section (statement 1066-1073, proof 1074-1087): a three-step equivalence chain whose each step is a direct application of a named lemma of the unit. H2: mechanical once the four lemmas are at hand, no new construction.
